summary: Nora's two unprompted halves stop guessing: the gate is told what she can actually call, and the proactive pass can look up who a nickname is.
details: The Relevance Gate decides whether a quiet room has anything Nora can serve, and was never told what she can do — its whole knowledge was a hand-written five-item list against 53 registered tools. It now receives her live read-only tool surface, derived from the registry on every start, so a tool added on master is a capability the gate knows about on the next deploy.
Measured cost of the old shape: 「知唔知聽朝會唔會落雨？」 scored no_go with confidence 0, while the gate's own instruction names the weather as something she can look up.

The proactive pass can now call lookup_person. Without it nothing answered 'who is this handle?' — group_members returns real names with no aliases beside them — so a note written in the group's nicknames sent one decide turn through six memory searches for the same answer before a guard stopped it.
participation.md no longer claims to hold the whole capability list; it keeps the judgement the registry cannot express — which kinds of ask are hers at all.
limitations: The digest adds roughly 840 tokens to every gate call, on every quiet window in every opted-in room.
Four members of the friends workspace still have no identity mapping, so some nicknames remain unresolvable whatever verb is granted.
Whether the capability gap or the shadow-held transcript caused the observed miss is not yet separated; issue #144 names the replay that would settle it.
